slot.brief: Compute real/imaginary parts of an expression of the form z + 1/z using conjugate and modulus relations.

stem: Let $z$ satisfy $|z|^2=13$, $z+\bar z=6$ and $\operatorname{Im}z<0$. Find the real and imaginary parts of $z+\dfrac{1}{z}$.

verdicts.working: Write z=x+iy. From z+\bar z=6, x=3; from |z|^2=13, y^2=4, and Im z<0 gives y=-2. Thus z=3-2i and 1/z=(3+2i)/13, so z+1/z=(42/13)-(24/13)i.

working:
$\operatorname{Re}z=3$, $|z|^2=13$, $\operatorname{Im}z<0\Rightarrow z=3-2i$; $\dfrac1z=\dfrac{\bar z}{|z|^2}=\dfrac{3+2i}{13}$; $z+\dfrac1z=\dfrac{42}{13}-\dfrac{24}{13}i$.

Independent check: Write z=x+iy. From z+\bar z=6, x=3; from |z|^2=13, y^2=4, and Im z<0 gives y=-2. Thus z=3-2i and 1/z=(3+2i)/13, so z+1/z=(42/13)-(24/13)i.
solution:
From $z+\bar z=6$, $\operatorname{Re}z=3$. Since $|z|^2=13$ and $\operatorname{Im}z<0$, $z=3-2i$.
$$\frac1z=\frac{\bar z}{|z|^2}=\frac{3+2i}{13},\qquad z+\frac1z=\frac{42}{13}-\frac{24}{13}i$$
Hence the real and imaginary parts are $\left(\frac{42}{13},-\frac{24}{13}\right)$.
